newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk parliament to widen Ciller graft vote probe.
newsitem.headline: Turk parliament to widen Ciller graft vote probe.

text.p: A Turkish parliamentary commission is to probe further into a disputed vote this week that decided against setting up a new inquiry into Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller on corruption charges, MPs said on Thursday.
"The objections are at a serious level and must be looked into," speaker Mustafa Kalemli told reporters. He said five MPs had been appointed to investigate claims of vote-rigging.
The opposition says two or three government MPs were counted as having voted for Ciller despite not being in attendance at Tuesday's ballot.
It also says one vote against Ciller, also the foreign minister, was found on the floor of the debating hall after the result was declared.
The vote could have caused a rift in the government if coalition partner Islamist Welfare Party MPs had swayed it against Ciller.
She had been accused of involvement in corruption at the state-run hotel and tourism company Turban.
Deputy speaker Yasin Hatipoglu originally announced Ciller had won the ballot by 247 to 242 but parliament officials later revised the number of votes in her favour to 244.
Former prime minister Ciller recently avoided being sent to the Supreme Court in three alleged corruption cases with the help of Welfare MPs who voted to drop the charges.
Most MPs of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare Party again backed Ciller in the latest vote but a group of around 20 defied the premier's orders to back her.
